hints: Look first at the vertical backbone on the left with three carbons. Is that a polysaccharide like glycogen or the 3-carbon alcohol glycerol?
Compare the three fatty acid tails on the right. Which ones have only single C-C bonds with maximum H atoms, and which one has a C=C double bond?
walkthrough:
**Spot the backbone**

Look at the left side of the diagram. You can see three CH groups linked vertically. That is glycerol, a 3-carbon alcohol, not glycogen which is a huge branched polysaccharide.

So we can already rule out any option mentioning glycogen.

**Check saturated versus unsaturated tails**

Now follow the three fatty acid chains to the right. The top two chains have only single bonds between carbons, with two H atoms on each carbon. That means they are saturated.

The bottom chain has one C=C double bond near the end, so it has fewer H atoms. That means it is monounsaturated. So we have 2 saturated and 1 unsaturated.

**Apply hydrolysis correctly**

Hydrolysis of an ester bond breaks it by USING water, not making water. The general reaction is:
$$triglyceride + 3H_2O \rightarrow glycerol + 3 \text{ fatty acids}$$
Water is a reactant used up to split the three ester bonds. It is not listed as a product of hydrolysis. Condensation to form the triglyceride would release water, but breaking it consumes water.

Putting it together: 1 glycerol + 2 saturated fatty acids + 1 unsaturated fatty acid. That is option B.

options.A: Incorrect because the backbone is glycerol, not glycogen, and only one tail is unsaturated, not three.
options.B: Correct. Hydrolysis splits the three ester bonds to release 1 glycerol, 2 saturated fatty acids (top two chains) and 1 unsaturated fatty acid (bottom chain with C=C).
options.C: Incorrect because it names glycogen instead of glycerol, even though the fatty acid count is right.
options.D: Incorrect because water is used up in hydrolysis, not produced, and the saturated to unsaturated count is reversed.
